title: Flat quotient presentation intersection under base change
statement: Let $R,B$ be commutative rings with an algebra map $R\to B$, let $F,M$ be $R$-modules, and let $q:F\to M$ be a surjective $R$-linear map. Let $I\subseteq R$ be an ideal and put $J=IB$. For an $R$-submodule $L\subseteq F$, write $L_B=\operatorname{im}(B\otimes_R L\to B\otimes_R F)$. Suppose $(R/I)\otimes_R M$ is flat over $R/I$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Then $(\ker q)_B\cap J(B\otimes_R F)\subseteq (\ker q\cap IF)_B+J(\ker q)_B$. No flatness or freeness of $F$ or $B$ is assumed.

source.place: Algebra, Tags 00MM (lemma-surjective-on-tor-one), 00MO (lemma-another-variant-local-criterion-flatness), and 00HL (lemma-flat-tor-zero); proof at presentation level by X3

proof.text: Set Q=R/I, J=IB, C=B/J. Let p be the Q-base change of q and V=ker p. The map e:ker q -> V sends l to 1 tensor l and is onto by right exactness and the surjectivity of F -> Q tensor_R F. Its kernel consists exactly of the relations lying in IF. The latter two facts follow from the quotient tensor equivalence and the kernel of the unit tensor map.

The exact sequence 0 -> V -> Q tensor F -> Q tensor M -> 0 has flat final term. Apply flat-quotient tensor injectivity with C over Q. Quotient-surjectivity identifies the Q and R tensor products of the Q-modules, yielding injectivity of C tensor_R V -> C tensor_R (Q tensor F).

Lift z in the displayed intersection to t in B tensor ker q. Reduction of z in C tensor F vanishes because z is in J times B tensor F. Commutation of the tensor maps and the preceding injectivity show that the reduction tc of t maps to zero in C tensor V. Right exactness of ker e -> ker q -> V produces s in C tensor ker e mapping to tc. Lift s to v in B tensor ker e using B -> C onto. Subtract its image vl from t; the difference lies in the kernel of B tensor ker q -> C tensor ker q, hence lifts to ker(B -> C) tensor ker q by right exactness.

The image of vl lies in the extension of ker q intersect IF by the kernel description of e. Tensor induction shows the image of t-vl is in J times the extension of ker q, since ker(B -> C)=J. Their sum is z, proving the inclusion.
